newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA's Corpoven sees growth in Latam, Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA's Corpoven sees growth in Latam, Caribbean.

text.p: Venezuela's Corpoven, a unit of state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), expects to concentrate increasingly on local markets in the Caribbean and South America over the next decade, company officials said Monday.
"The fundamental area of growth at the moment is in Latin America and the Caribbean," Corpoven vice-president Ronald Pantin told reporters during a luncheon.
In 1996 Corpoven exported an average of 139,000 barrels per day of crude to the Caribbean and 126,000 bpd to South America, principally Brazil.

According to figures presented by Corpoven President Guillermo Archila, crude sales to the Caribbean are seen growing by 164 percent to 367,000 bpd by the year 2006. Sales to South America are seen increasing by 61 percent to 203,000 bpd over the same period.

Corpoven's biggest market, however, remains the United States which bought an average of 602,000 bpd in 1996. Sales to the Unites States are seen growing by 82 percent to 1.096 million bpd by 2006, Archila said.
Sales to Europe, already low at 23,000 bpd in 1996 are seen slipping to just 10,000 bpd over the next decade, he said.
